content: Theanine is an amino acid that is naturally found in tea, specifically in infusions of Camellia sinensis. It is structurally related to glutamine and has the ability to cross the blood-brain barrier. Due to its capacity to enter the brain, theanine exhibits psychoactive properties. Theanine has been demonstrated to reduce both mental and physical stress, and it may induce a state of relaxation. It is hypothesized that these effects are mediated through an increase in the production of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a key inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain. Additionally, theanine has been shown to elevate levels of serotonin, dopamine, and GABA in the brain. It also exhibits micromolar affinities for AMPA, kainate, and NMDA receptors, which are critical components of excitatory neurotransmission. In studies involving spontaneously hypertensive mice, the administration of theanine significantly reduced levels of 5-hydroxyindole in the brain, a compound associated with serotonin metabolism. Researchers have also proposed that theanine may inhibit excitotoxicity caused by excessive glutamic acid activity, which can lead to neuronal damage. Theanine has been found to promote the production of alpha brain waves, which are associated with a relaxed yet alert mental state. Experimental studies on test rats have shown that even when administered in repeated, extremely high doses, theanine causes minimal to no harmful psychological or physical effects. L-theanine may also enhance the immune system's response to infections. It has been observed to boost the disease-fighting capacity of gamma delta T cells, a subset of immune cells. A study conducted in 2003 by Brigham and Women’s Hospital involved a four-week trial with 11 coffee drinkers and 10 tea drinkers, each consuming 600 milliliters of coffee or black tea daily. Blood sample analysis revealed that the production of antibacterial proteins was up to five times higher in the tea drinkers, indicating a stronger immune response. Recently, tea companies have highlighted the natural presence of L-theanine in their products as part of their marketing campaigns. They emphasize that L-theanine enhances the production of alpha brain waves, further promoting its benefits for relaxation and mental clarity.
